question: What should an agency's test plan include to reduce testing bias and verify both test design and human control?
draft:
An agency's test plan should address bias mitigation in the testing process, human verification of test design, and controllability testing, drawing on the Australian Government AI Technical Standard's Evaluate section.

**Bias mitigation in testing (Statement 26, Criterion 91)**
Agencies must mitigate bias in the testing process, which includes differentiating test data for formal testing from data used during model development, ensuring test subjects are not involved in the development of the SUT, providing testers and developers a degree of independence from each other, using test-driven development (designing test cases based on requirements and prior to implementing data, models, and non-AI components), and conducting peer reviews, bias awareness training, and documenting test-related decisions and processes [4].

**Test criteria approaches (Statement 26, Criterion 92)**
Agencies must define test criteria approaches, which determine whether a test case has passed or failed by comparing actual output with expected output; this includes considering statistical techniques (repeating test cases, defining thresholds, minimum values, and average efficiency in probabilistic and non-deterministic systems) [4].

**Human verification of test design (Statement 27, Criterion 95)**
Agencies must undertake human verification of test design and implementation for correctness, consistency, and completeness [1].

**Controllability testing (Statement 27, Criterion 97)**
Agencies must perform controllability testing to verify human oversight and control, and system control requirements [1].

**Related testing elements in Statement 27**
Functional performance testing must verify the correctness of the SUT as per pre-defined metrics, including testing for fairness and bias to inform affirmative actions; for off-the-shelf systems, benchmark testing using industry-standard benchmark suites and comparisons with competing AI systems should be considered [1]. Explainability and transparency testing must be performed as per requirements, involving testing that AI outputs are understandable for the target audience (ensuring diversity of test subjects and representativeness of the target population) and that the right information is available for the right user [1].

**Evidence gaps**
The provided excerpts do not establish a single consolidated "test plan" document or template; the requirements above are drawn from separate criteria within Statements 26 and 27. The excerpts also do not establish specific deadlines, approval authorities, or a prescribed format for documenting the test plan.

child_citations.section_title: Statement 23: Validate, assess, and update model
child_citations.title: Australian Government AI Technical Standard
child_citations.quote:
Statement 23: Validate, assess, and update model Agencies must: Criterion 84: Set techniques to validate AI trained models. There are multiple qualitative and quantitative techniques and tools for model validation, informed by the AI system success criteria (see Design section), including: o correct classifications, predictions or forecasts, and factual correctness and relevance o identify between positive and negative instances, and distinguish between classes

o benchmarking o consistency in responses, clarity and coherence o source attribution o data-centric validation approaches for GenAI models. Criterion 85: Evaluate the model against training boundaries. Evaluation considerations include: o poor or degraded performance of the model o change of AI context or operational setting o data retention policies o model retention policies. Criterion 86: Evaluate the model for bias, implement and test bias mitigations. This includes: o using suitable tools that test and discover unwarranted associations between an algorithm’s protected input features and its output o evaluating performance across suitable and intersectional dimensions o checking if bias could be managed through updating the training data (see Statement 18) o implementing bias mitigation thresholds that can be configured post-deployment o implementing pre-processing or post-processing techniques such as disparate impact remover, equalised odds post-processing, content filtering, and RAG. Agencies should: Criterion 87: Identify relevant model refinement methods.

child_citations.title: Australian Government AI Technical Standard
child_citations.quote:
Criterion 69: Manage bias in the data.

Techniques for agencies to manage and mitigate problematic bias in their model dataset includes: o data collection analysis – examining how data was generated and verified, and checking the methodologies used to ensure the data is diverse and represents the real population o data source analysis – investigating limitations and assumptions around the origin of the data o data diversity – determining various demographics, sources and types of data, inclusion and exclusion considerations o statistical testing – determining the likelihood of the population being accurately represented in the data o class imbalance – analysing data for class imbalance before using it to train classification models, and applying relevant data and algorithm techniques and metrics, such as precision or F1-score, to address this o outlier detection – identifying outliers or unusual data points in the data and ensuring they are handled appropriately o exploratory data analysis – using descriptive statistics and data visualisation tools to identify patterns and discrepancies o removing any irrelevant data from the training data that does not improve the performance of the model o ensuring that any sensitive and protected data are retained in the test datasets for the purpose of evaluating for bias o data augmentation – deploying measures to address the completeness of the model dataset, through supplementary data collection or synthetic data generation o transparency – identifying bias and where it originated from through transparency on data
